result.summary: The cause is real: uncancelled 10-page walks per keystroke burn incident.io's 60-per-minute list limit. The PR only shrinks the walk, so 429s and the Error Tracking issue still occur. It also cuts name-search coverage to 750 incidents without saying so plainly, and the tests don't exercise a 429.

problems.title: Symptom reduced, not fixed
problems.detail: A 429 still gives an empty picker and an error-level log, only less often. The limit is shared per workspace connection, and 3 pages per query can still exceed 60 per minute.

problems.title: Silent loss of search coverage
problems.detail: Name search drops from the newest 2,500 incidents to 750. Older incidents become unfindable by name, and the description says it 'still covers' them.

problems.title: 429 treated as an internal error
problems.detail: A rate limit is an expected condition but is logged at error and mapped to internalError, so Error Tracking keeps firing. Nothing returns a rate-limited domain error or a partial result.

problems.title: Tests restate the implementation
problems.detail: The page-count tests assert the constant. No test covers a 429 or concurrent queries, search terms with whitespace, or a match that only exists beyond page 3.

problems.title: Unrelated and misleading changes
problems.detail: The term is now trimmed before matching, which changes behaviour. The helper extraction and cursor rewrite are churn. SEARCH_MATCH_LIMIT does not cap the number of results, only when paging stops.

result.betterFix: Cache the incident list briefly per connection and share one in-flight list call across concurrent searches, so typing does not multiply calls. Map 429 to an expected rate-limited domain error (logged below error, or returning the cached or partial list) instead of internalError. If a page cap stays, state the coverage cut openly and keep the existing cap unless the team accepts it.
